opportunities.title: W.K. Kellogg Foundation - Mexico programme (Chiapas Highlands & inner Yucatan Peninsula): rolling Letter of Inquiry for food systems / seed-land-water access / climate adaptation / agroecology
opportunities.program: WKKF Mexico - Health (Food Systems, Community Water Management) and Family Economic Security (coffee, honey, milpa, backyard gardens)
opportunities.deadline_text: "Our application process is always open." "In general, we don't have specific grantmaking cycles or deadlines."
opportunities.funding_text: Not specified on official pages (award size determined case by case after invited proposal).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Organizations whose work fits WKKF priorities; "We are unable to make grants for individuals, capital investments, political parties or candidates." No formal eligibility list on the grantseekers page.
opportunities.eligible_countries: USA; Mexico (25 municipalities in Chiapas Highlands and inner Yucatan Peninsula: Yucatan, Campeche, Quintana Roo); Haiti (central and southwest).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Official pages do not restrict applicant nationality or legal form, but grants are place-based and community-led in 25 specific municipalities. Secondary sources report a WKKF-UNDP Mexico partnership in 40 southeastern communities (UNDP page returned 403, unverified), suggesting international organizations can be grantees. Most realistic route: Alliance as technical partner to a local community organization or to the locally managed Agroecology Fund of the Yucatan Peninsula, or a direct LOI for a co-designed project; confirm with the WKKF Concierge Desk whether CIAT/Bioversity can be direct grantees.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Register in WKKF's Fluxx system and submit a Letter of Inquiry; formal proposal only by invitation.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Mexico grantmaking concentrated on 25 municipalities in Chiapas Highlands and inner Yucatan Peninsula.
opportunities.consortium_details: Not required; strong emphasis on community-led, Indigenous-knowledge-based partnerships.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Food systems: "We are supporting communities to secure access to seed, land and water to advance food sovereignty and enhance adaptation, as well as helping get healthy, locally produced food into schools and local and regional markets." Agroecology: "We are committed to supporting agroecology as a movement that recognizes Indigenous knowledge". Economic security: agriculture, especially coffee, honey, milpa, backyard gardens, animal husbandry. Also community water management.
opportunities.required_documents: Letter of Inquiry (short, high-level description) via Fluxx; full proposal if invited.
opportunities.application_procedure: Register in Fluxx -> submit LOI (instructions in English, Spanish, Haitian Creole) -> WKKF responds within ~30 business days -> invited proposals reviewed in ~60 business days. Questions: conciergedesk@wkkf.org.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate adaptation of milpa/coffee/honey systems, agrobiodiversity and water access are relevant, but WKKF funds community-led action and equity outcomes; RS/AI/crop modelling would only be a supporting component (e.g., participatory climate-risk maps, milpa suitability).
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Large foundation with multi-year, place-based commitments in Mexico; Alliance has milpa/agrobiodiversity and coffee-climate expertise in Mesoamerica; but narrow geography and community-led ethos limit research-staff funding.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Feasible only with established local community partners in Yucatan/Chiapas.
opportunities.recommendation: Only funder among those checked with an always-open official application route touching LAC climate adaptation. Pursue only if a Yucatan/Chiapas community partner can lead; frame the Alliance role as climate-risk/agrobiodiversity science service to community food sovereignty. Do not expect it to fund an EO/AI research agenda.
opportunities.potential_partners: Agroecology Fund of the Yucatan Peninsula; UNDP Mexico (reported WKKF partner); local milpa/apiculture/coffee cooperatives; ECOSUR; Alliance Mesoamerica agrobiodiversity team
opportunities.next_action: Email conciergedesk@wkkf.org asking whether an international organization (CIAT/Bioversity) can be a direct grantee in the Mexico programme and whether staff costs are allowable; in parallel identify a Yucatan community partner to co-author a Fluxx LOI.
